$comment: Single source of truth for CI test sharding. Read by BOTH:
- scripts/check-shard-coverage.mjs  (proves the patterns partition the suite)
- .github/workflows/ci-tests.yml    (builds the job matrix via fromJSON)
so the two can never drift.
WHY WE SHARD: every suite retains ~29 MB that is never released (each one
imports the whole app). Measured: 218 MB at suite 1 -> 2,814 MB at suite 90.
All 167 suites in one process projects to ~5,060 MB against Node 20's ~4,096 MB
default heap, so the single-job CI OOMs deterministically, not intermittently.
Each shard here peaks 3-5x under that ceiling.
WHY ONE JOB PER SHARD (and NOT jest --maxWorkers): all suites in a Jest process
share ONE database and isolate via per-test transactional rollback. Concurrent
workers would interleave transactions on the same rows. The unit of parallelism
must therefore be one database per Jest process => one per CI job.
Do not raise maxWorkers in jest.config.js to 'speed this up'.
DB ISOLATION IS FREE: tests/setup/envguard.js reads TEST_RUN_ID before falling
back to GITHUB_RUN_ID, so the workflow sets TEST_RUN_ID=ci_<run_id>_<shard> and
each job gets its own hospitality_test_* database with no harness change.
ADDING A TEST FILE: if it does not match exactly one pattern below, the
coverage-guard job fails the build. That is deliberate - it is the only thing
standing between us and a new suite silently never running in CI. Fix the
pattern or add a shard; do not weaken the guard.
PATTERNS are JS regexes matched UNANCHORED against the repo-relative POSIX
path, which is exactly how Jest's --testPathPatterns treats them. Do not add
a leading ^ : Jest matches against the ABSOLUTE path and the anchor would
select nothing (silently green, zero tests run).
SPLIT: a domain too large for one shard is divided by Jest's own --shard=i/n,
which is exhaustive and balanced by construction. The guard only checks the
pattern layer; Jest guarantees full coverage within it.
